how: Three months before the S&P 500. The Russell 2000 fell 36.9% to 8 October.
The index fell 19.3% in the next 31 sessions.

t: Russia devalues and defaults on domestic debt
how: S&P 500 +2.0% that day to 1083.67. The selling came over the following two weeks.
SPY traded 2.8 times its 50-day average, two sessions before the closing low.
The largest one-day fall of the decline. The index rose 3.9% the next session.

t: Follow-through day, fifth session after the low
how: +5.1% to 1023.46 on higher volume. The rally lasted to 23 September and was then almost fully given back.

t: LTCM rescue: 14 firms put in about $3.6bn
how: S&P 500 +3.5% to 1066.09. The New York Fed arranged the takeover and lent nothing.

t: Fed cuts 0.25 points; the market wanted more
how: Flat on the day, then −3.1% and −3.0% over the next two sessions.
The yen had risen 14% in two days. Small-company and Nasdaq indices closed at new lows; the S&P 500 held 0.2% above its August close. VIX 45.7.
Second cut of 0.25 points. The start of the rise to new highs.

t: Corporate credit spread peaks at 2.77 points
how: One week after the intraday low. Spreads stayed wide into year-end while stocks rose.
S&P 500 +0.3% to 1139.32. The last cut; increases resumed in June 1999.
Six weeks after the intraday low. Large technology stocks led; small companies were still far below their April high.
